title: A stored field's expression is not filled in for existing rows on a hosted tenant: switching a formula to a stored number leaves old rows NULL and a dataset sum silently reads 0 (#32443 follow-up)
body:
domain:spec#4 · marchtian · session_017ihL2gENvvRYHmL5nFTF5x

Filing gate: ① product defect (user-visible), measured by the #32443 card thread (step-1 measurement, tree `1ff9f80d`, sqlite, real ObjectQL + AnalyticsServicePlugin). ⛔ Not a claim. Triage sets the grade and the lane.
Reader: the server / CLI owner of `os migrate stored-expressions` (`packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/stored-expressions.ts`) and the metadata save path that adds or changes a stored field's `expression`.
Dedupe: `is:issue is:open stored-expressions backfill` → 1 hit (a seat post); none on this.
reach: #32443 (maintainer ruling B, "a computed value can be totalled") is delivered by a stored field that carries an `expression` (computed on every write and kept in a column). The refusal's remedy now points authors there. An author following it on an app that already has data replaces a `formula` with `type: 'number'` + the same `expression`. In the measurement every existing row stayed `NULL`, so the dataset `sum` read 0 where the true value was 6, with no error. Changing an existing stored expression likewise leaves old values uncomputed. A boot warning exists, and `os migrate stored-expressions --apply` (and `--changed`) fills them, but it needs a direct database URL, which a hosted tenant does not have. The metadata save door gives no warning either.
Related: #32443 (Blocked-by only for the wording; the defect stands on main today for any stored expression added to a populated object)

## Ask

Give a hosted tenant a way to fill a stored expression for existing rows when the field is added or its expression changes: at save time (a job the save starts), or through an entry the hosted tier can reach. Until rows are filled, the field's aggregates should not read as complete numbers: a warning at save, or the read path refusing or marking them. The lane rules the shape. Pin the card's case: formula → stored number on a populated object, then sum.
